text:
maya: heads-up — noticed a batch of requests that should have billed to customer-project but ended up on org-default. telemetry shows project claim dropped during proxy fallback :thinking_face:
adrian: timeline? is this the SA->proxy exchange path we rolled last week? :eyes:
maya: yes, started around 10:12 UTC yesterday. looks like when proxy couldn't introspect service-account claim it rewrote origin to org:  `origin: org/789` instead of `origin: org/789/project/222/sa/infra`
kevin: that sounds like the origin cascade we discussed — fallback rule is org > project > sa when claims missing. but we intended to preserve whatever precise origin we had on request.
sam: are we sure the claim was actually missing and not dropped by the edge? we saw intermittent 401s from the token-introspect service during the window. infra-bot: token-introspect v2.3.0 deployed 2025-11-04T09:58Z, host pool rotated at 10:05Z.
adrian: if introspect failed, our proxy's current behavior canonicalizes to org-only to keep routing simple. that has the unintended billing attribution effect.
maya: yep — customer reported spike in org-level unit_usage. chart attached (pasted): `usage.org/789.tokens = +12%` while project/222 shows -12%
kevin: options: 1) make proxy leave original header untouched on introspect error (preferable), 2) change canonicalization to prefer project if request had project-scoped headers, 3) mark those traces and exclude from billing until we replay fix — but replay is hard.
sam: note: changing proxy to leave headers could leak stale claims if upstream is misbehaving. we need safe guard, maybe `x-origin: original` + `x-origin-asserted: false` so console/billing can decide.
maya: +1 for `x-origin-asserted` approach. we should also add telemetry tag so we can filter these in dashboards: `auth.origin_resolution: fallback-introspect-error`
adrian: implementation detail: proxy already attaches `auth.resolution` for normal paths. adding another enum value easy. billing side needs a deterministic rule: either bill org when asserted=false or don't bill and emit invoice-adj flag. ops, thoughts?
kevin: my preference: bill to the most specific asserted identity; if none asserted, route to org but mark `asserted=false` and increment a counter `billing.attribution_uncertain`. Then finance can run weekly checks.
maya: will this break SLA for dedicated customers who require strict project billing? (we have a few customers that refused org-level fallback)
sam: dedicated customers should get stricter behavior behind a flag — `x-billing-fallback: deny` header enforced at proxy. Default remains tolerant.
adrian: console UX: we need to surface these uncertain attributions in the per-route dashboard and allow toggles for `deny fallback` per-customer. devex: can we add a small affordance in the console — badge on route showing "attribution uncertain (n events)" and a link to sample traces?
devex: yes — small telemetry endpoint exists. will need new columns: `attribution_uncertain_count` and a filter by `auth.origin_resolution` values.
maya: quick implementation plan: (1) proxy: add `x-origin-asserted` + new `auth.origin_resolution` enum + header pass-through; (2) billing: count `billing.attribution_uncertain`, don't auto-charge adjustments; (3) console: expose badge + trace links; (4) add canary flag `billing_fallback_strict` for Dedicated customers.
kevin: timeline? we should hotfix proxy change to preserve header ASAP patch then ship full telemetry next week.
adrian: I'll do the proxy change (small PR). will also add tests to ensure we don't accidentally accept forged `x-origin-asserted`.
sam: remember to harden header acceptance: only accept `x-origin-asserted` from trusted proxies (internal network) and require signature for cross-region proxies.
maya: good catch. add to spec: header must be signed or coming from trusted CIDR.
infra-bot: canary rollout checklist generated: patch -> unit tests -> staging rollout -> 10% prod -> 100% prod.
adrian: ok starting a PR now, pinging infra for CIDR list. link when ready. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — and please add a quick retro blurb in incidents if we confirm billing impact so finance/customer-ops can reach out.
kevin: will follow up with a short note for accounts.
maya: for trace of the problem window: `first_message_ts` 1797772468 -> `last_message_ts` 1797772590 (keeping metadata aligned).
